findings: REST getAccessToken documents apiKey, not MCP Token.
Official parser supports MCP@userId@CJ:accessToken; source notes treating MCP format as API Key caused 1600005.
Direct-token context returns suffix without refresh/exchange; http client sends it as CJ-Access-Token.
Source does not prove deployed remote revision, token issuance side effects, credential validity or owner account binding.
MCP search_products invokes GET product/listV2, useful catalog evidence; wrapper has retry loop and does not provide the prepared strict one-attempt bound.
MCP account label is supplied by credential URL, not independent provider account proof.
recommendation: Prefer separate newly issued MCP direct credential with a narrowly adapted standalone REST GET verifier; do not retrieve or relocate production secret. No API-key exchange. Conditional on secure owner provisioning and reviewed single-run workflow.
